A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in general, data harmonization is not trivial, and that the effect of data manipulation on the uncertainty budget is often underestimated.

, while the information content of a dataset is preserved in a harmonization process, the uncertainty budget of a data comparison is changed by the harmonization operations, in particular if prior information or retrieval differences are accounted for.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the information content and uncertainty of the data comparison is affected by the harmonization process in ways that are not always intuitive.
, for data comparisons, the uncertainty budget should be assessed by considering the full chain of operations from the original observations to the data product.
the effect of harmonization and mismatching operations on the uncertainty budget can be substantial and needs to be considered in the interpretation of data comparisons.
